questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of the following cannot be the order of a row-matrix?
questions.solution: A row matrix has exactly one row, i.e. order 1 × n. A 2 × 1 matrix is a column matrix.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Which of the following properties is/are true for two matrices of suitable orders?
(i) (A + B)′ = A′ + B′  (ii) (A − B)′ = B′ − A′  (iii) (AB)′ = A′B′  (iv) (kAB)′ = kB′A′ (k is a scalar)
questions.solution: (A − B)′ = A′ − B′ and (AB)′ = B′A′, so (ii) and (iii) are false; (i) and (iv) are true.

questions.solution: (A − B)′ = A′ − B′ = −A + B = −(A − B). The others are symmetric in general.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): In an experiment of throwing an unbiased die, the probability of getting a prime number given that the number appearing on the die is odd is 2/3.
Reason (R): For any two events A and B, P(A|B) = P(A ∪ B)/P(B).
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Odd outcomes {1, 3, 5}; primes among them {3, 5}: probability 2/3, so A is true. R is false: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Lines given by x = py + q, z = ry + s and x = p′y + q′, z = r′y + s′ are perpendicular to each other when pp′ + rr′ = 1.
Reason (R): Two lines r = a₁ + λb₁ and r = a₂ + μb₂ are perpendicular to each other if b₁ · b₂ = 0.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: The direction ratios are (p, 1, r) and (p′, 1, r′). Perpendicular means pp′ + 1 + rr′ = 0, i.e. pp′ + rr′ = −1, so A is false. R is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Check whether the function f(x) defined as f(x) = |x − 3|/(2(x − 3)) for x < 3 and (x − 6)/6 for x ≥ 3 is continuous at x = 3 or not.
questions.solution: For x < 3, |x − 3| = −(x − 3), so f(x) = −1/2 and the left-hand limit is −1/2. f(3) = (3 − 6)/6 = −1/2 and the right-hand limit is also −1/2. All three are equal, so f is continuous at x = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If √3(x² + y²) = 4xy, then find dy/dx at (1/2, √3/2).
questions.solution: Differentiating: √3(2x + 2y y′) = 4y + 4x y′, so y′ = (2y − √3x)/(√3y − 2x). At (1/2, √3/2): numerator √3 − √3/2 = √3/2, denominator 3/2 − 1 = 1/2, so dy/dx = √3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A room freshener bottle in the shape of an inverted cone sprays the perfume at regular intervals such that the volume of the perfume in the bottle decreases at the steady rate of 1 mm³/min. Find the rate at which the level of perfume is dropping at an instant when the level of perfume in the bottle is 10 mm, if the semi-vertical angle of the conical bottle is π/6.
questions.solution: With level h, radius r = h tan(π/6) = h/√3, so V = (1/3)πr²h = πh³/9. dV/dt = (πh²/3) dh/dt = −1. At h = 10: dh/dt = −3/(100π). The level drops at 3/(100π) mm/min.

questions.text: Find the vector of magnitude 14 in the direction of QP, where P and Q are the points (1, 3, 2) and (−1, 0, 8) respectively.
questions.solution: QP = P − Q = 2i + 3j − 6k with |QP| = 7. Required vector = 14 × (2i + 3j − 6k)/7 = 4i + 6j − 12k.

questions.solution: Diagonals: a + b = 4i − 2j + 4k, length √(16 + 4 + 16) = 6; a − b = 2i − 2j, length √8 = 2√2.

questions.text: If I₁ = ∫ from −π/4 to π/4 of dx/(1 + cos 2x) and I₂ = ∫ from −1/2 to 1/2 of |x| dx, then show that I₁ − 4I₂ = 0.
questions.solution: 1 + cos 2x = 2cos²x, so I₁ = ½[tan x] from −π/4 to π/4 = ½(1 + 1) = 1. I₂ = 2∫₀^(1/2) x dx = 2 × 1/8 = 1/4. Hence I₁ − 4I₂ = 1 − 1 = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation x² dy/dx = x² + xy + y².
questions.solution: dy/dx = 1 + y/x + (y/x)² is homogeneous. Put y = vx: v + x dv/dx = 1 + v + v², so dv/(1 + v²) = dx/x. Integrating, tan⁻¹v = log|x| + C, i.e. tan⁻¹(y/x) = log|x| + C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation xy dy/dx = (x + 2)(y + 2), given that y(1) = −1.
questions.solution: Separate: y/(y + 2) dy = (x + 2)/x dx, i.e. (1 − 2/(y + 2)) dy = (1 + 2/x) dx. Integrating: y − 2 log|y + 2| = x + 2 log|x| + C. With x = 1, y = −1: −1 = 1 + C, so C = −2. Particular solution: y − 2 log|y + 2| = x + 2 log|x| − 2.

questions.solution: The lines x + y = 7 and 2x − 3y = −6 meet at (3, 4). The bounded feasible region has corner points (0, 0), (7, 0), (3, 4) and (0, 2), where Z = 0, 91, −21 and −30. Minimum Z = −30 at (0, 2).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The probability of simultaneous occurrence of at least one of the two events X and Y is a. If the probability that exactly one of the events X, Y occurs is b, prove that P(X′) + P(Y′) = 2 − 2a + b.
questions.solution: P(X ∪ Y) = P(X) + P(Y) − P(X ∩ Y) = a and P(exactly one) = P(X) + P(Y) − 2P(X ∩ Y) = b. Subtracting, P(X ∩ Y) = a − b, so P(X) + P(Y) = 2a − b. Hence P(X′) + P(Y′) = 2 − (2a − b) = 2 − 2a + b.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation R is defined on Z, the set of integers, as R = {(x, y) : |x − y| is divisible by a prime number p, x, y ∈ Z}. Check whether R is an equivalence relation or not.
questions.solution: Reflexive: |x − x| = 0 is divisible by p. Symmetric: |y − x| = |x − y|. Transitive: if x − y = pk and y − z = pm, then x − z = p(k + m), so |x − z| is divisible by p. R is an equivalence relation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A function f : R − {3/5} → R − {3/5} is defined as f(x) = (3x + 2)/(5x − 3). Show that f is one-one and onto.
questions.solution: One-one: (3a + 2)/(5a − 3) = (3b + 2)/(5b − 3) gives 15ab − 9a + 10b − 6 = 15ab − 9b + 10a − 6, so 19a = 19b and a = b. Onto: for y ≠ 3/5, solving y = (3x + 2)/(5x − 3) gives x = (3y + 2)/(5y − 3), which is defined and is not 3/5 (that would need 3y + 2 = 3y − 9/5). Then f(x) = y, so f is onto.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If [[3, −1, sin 3x], [−7, 4, cos 2x], [−11, 7, 2]] is a singular matrix, then find all values of x where x ∈ [0, π/2].
questions.solution: Expanding along the third column: sin 3x(−49 + 44) − cos 2x(21 − 11) + 2(12 − 7) = −5 sin 3x − 10 cos 2x + 10 = 0, i.e. sin 3x + 2cos 2x = 2. With s = sin x: 3s − 4s³ + 2 − 4s² = 2, so s(4s² + 4s − 3) = 0, giving s = 0, 1/2 or −3/2. In [0, π/2]: x = 0 or x = π/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If x = cos t, y = cos mt, prove that (1 − x²) d²y/dx² − x dy/dx + m²y = 0.
questions.solution: dy/dx = (−m sin mt)/(−sin t) = m sin mt/sin t, so √(1 − x²) dy/dx = m sin mt. Differentiating w.r.t. x: √(1 − x²) y″ − x y′/√(1 − x²) = m² cos mt · dt/dx = −m² y/√(1 − x²). Multiplying by √(1 − x²): (1 − x²)y″ − xy′ + m²y = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Check whether the lines given by (x − 1)/2 = (y − 2)/3 = (z − 3)/4 and (x − 4)/5 = (y − 1)/2 = z are parallel or not. If parallel, find the distance between them, otherwise find their point of intersection, if the lines are intersecting.
questions.solution: Directions (2, 3, 4) and (5, 2, 1) are not proportional, so the lines are not parallel. Points: (1 + 2λ, 2 + 3λ, 3 + 4λ) and (4 + 5μ, 1 + 2μ, μ). From z: μ = 3 + 4λ; then y: 2 + 3λ = 7 + 8λ, so λ = −1 and μ = −1. x: 1 − 2 = −1 and 4 − 5 = −1, consistent. The lines intersect at (−1, −1, −1).

How many subscribers will discontinue after an increase of ₹x in the annual fee?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of ₹3,00,000, two second prizes of ₹2,00,000 each and three third prizes of ₹50,000 each. A total of 1,00,000 jackpot tickets, each costing ₹100, were sold, raising a fund of ₹1,00,00,000. Rohan bought one ticket.

What is the probability that the person wins at least ₹2,00,000?
questions.solution: Three tickets win ₹2,00,000 or more (one first and two second prizes): 3/1,00,000 = 0.00003.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of ₹3,00,000, two second prizes of ₹2,00,000 each and three third prizes of ₹50,000 each. A total of 1,00,000 jackpot tickets, each costing ₹100, were sold, raising a fund of ₹1,00,00,000. Rohan bought one ticket.

What is the probability that the person does not win any amount?
questions.solution: Six tickets win a prize, so P(no prize) = 99,994/1,00,000 = 0.99994.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of ₹3,00,000, two second prizes of ₹2,00,000 each and three third prizes of ₹50,000 each. A total of 1,00,000 jackpot tickets, each costing ₹100, were sold, raising a fund of ₹1,00,00,000. Rohan bought one ticket.

In another jackpot, Rohan also bought a ticket having a prize money of ₹5,00,000. The chances of winning that jackpot are 1 in 1,00,000. Find the probability that he wins on exactly one of the tickets.
questions.solution: P(win on first) = 6/10⁵ and P(win on second) = 1/10⁵, independently. P(exactly one) = (6/10⁵)(1 − 1/10⁵) + (1 − 6/10⁵)(1/10⁵) = 7/10⁵ − 12/10¹⁰ = 0.0000699988 (portal's answer, treating any prize on the first ticket as a win).

questions.text:
Roundabouts are often made on busy roads to ease the traffic and avoid red lights. One such roundabout is made such that the equation representing its boundary is C₁ : x² + y² = 64. There is a circular pond with a fountain in the middle of the roundabout whose equation is C₂ : x² + y² = 4.

Represent the given equations C₁ and C₂ with the help of a diagram.
questions.solution: Two concentric circles centred at the origin: C₁ with radius 8 and C₂ with radius 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Roundabouts are often made on busy roads to ease the traffic and avoid red lights. One such roundabout is made such that the equation representing its boundary is C₁ : x² + y² = 64. There is a circular pond with a fountain in the middle of the roundabout whose equation is C₂ : x² + y² = 4.

Using integration, find the area of the region covered by the roundabout.
questions.solution: Area = 4∫₀⁸ √(64 − x²) dx = 4[(x/2)√(64 − x²) + 32 sin⁻¹(x/8)]₀⁸ = 4 × 16π = 64π square units. (Leaving out the pond, the area is 64π − 4π = 60π.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Roundabouts are often made on busy roads to ease the traffic and avoid red lights. One such roundabout is made such that the equation representing its boundary is C₁ : x² + y² = 64. There is a circular pond with a fountain in the middle of the roundabout whose equation is C₂ : x² + y² = 4.

Using integration, find the area of the region covered by the circular pond.
questions.solution: Area = 4∫₀² √(4 − x²) dx = 4[(x/2)√(4 − x²) + 2 sin⁻¹(x/2)]₀² = 4 × π = 4π square units.
